//: ETicketsGo customer web (Next.js standalone). Root Directory stays '/'. NO migrations here — the API service owns them. NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL is INLINED INTO THE BUNDLE AT BUILD TIME: the Dockerfile declares it as an ARG and Railway passes service variables as Docker build args, so it MUST be set on this service BEFORE the first build and a change to it requires a rebuild+redeploy, not just a restart. That also means the web image is environment-specific by construction (same commit, different public API URL) while the api/worker images are environment-neutral — see docs/deployment/RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md 'Promotion'. /api/health is a static Next route handler (no DB/Redis/API calls), which is the correct liveness signal for the web tier. Railway injects PORT; the standalone server reads PORT + HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 from the image ENV defaults.
